en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Ninth Chapter
The Discourse on Thoughts Following Upon Thought:
Is all consciousness accompanied by thought?
Yes, it is.
Every state of consciousness is accompanied by sustained application, accompanied by zest, accompanied by pleasure, accompanied by pain, accompanied by mental joy,
accompanied by mental grief, accompanied by equanimity, accompanied by faith, accompanied by energy,
accompanied by mindfulness, accompanied by concentration, accompanied by wisdom, accompanied by lust, accompanied by hatred … [and so on].
Is it not the case that all consciousness is accompanied by lack of moral dread (*anottappa*)?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is all consciousness accompanied by applied thought (*vitakka*)?
“Yes.
“But is there not a concentration that is without initial application and consists of sustained application alone?
“Yes.”
If there is concentration that is without applied thought and consists of sustained thought alone, then indeed, it should not be said:
"All consciousness is accompanied by applied thought.
Is it the case that all consciousness is accompanied by applied thought?
“Yes.
“But is there not concentration that is without initial application and without sustained application?
“Yes.”
If there is concentration that is without applied thought and without sustained thought, then indeed it should not be said:
"All consciousness is accompanied by applied thought.
Is it the case that all consciousness is accompanied by applied thought?
“Yes, [they are].
“But have not three kinds of concentration been spoken of by the Blessed One:

‘concentration with applied thought and sustained thought, concentration without applied thought and with sustained thought only, and concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought’?”
“Yes.
“If three kinds of concentration have been spoken of by the Blessed One—

concentration with directed thought and evaluation, concentration without directed thought and with only evaluation, and concentration without directed thought and without evaluation— then surely it should not be said [that there is only one kind].”
“All consciousness is accompanied by applied thought.
The Discussion on Being Accompanied by Applied Thought is finished.
